In eukaryotic cells, the selection of origin sites occurs during the G1 phase of the cell cycle. During this time, there are many origins that have been pre-selected and remain silent until the cell enters the S phase. Once the cell has entered the S phase, the selected origins become activated and initiate DNA replication. It is important that only one origin site is activated at a time as if multiple sites are active, it can lead to genomic instability. This instability can result in mutations which may cause diseases such as cancer. Therefore, each ddNTP acts as a termination signal for its complementary base. Since these bases are added in sequence, this allows the order of the bases to be determined. Fluorescent dyes are attached to the ddNTPs so that they can be detected and their sequence determined by capillary electrophoresis. β-oxidation converts fatty acids into two carbon fragments (acetyl-CoA) and a NADH molecule. This process occurs in the mitochondria, as this is where the enzymes necessary for β-oxidation are located, and ATP is generated by the electron transport chain. In order to repeat the cycle of β-oxidation the NAD+ must be regenerated to NADH and then to NAD+ again. This occurs via the FAD stripping system. The FAD stripping system involves FAD being stripped of an H atom and then the resulting FADH2 being used to reduce NAD+ to NADH. The FAD that has lost its H atom is then available to strip another H atom from Coenzyme A (CoA), forming FAD and FA-CoA respectively. The reaction between FAD and CoA is catalyzed by LCAT (Lysine-CoA-ATPase). The FAD stripping system allows β-oxidation to continue. If there was no FAD, the NAD+ would not be reduced to NADH and therefore the cycle could not continue. The lack of availability of CoA would also prevent the formation of Acetyl-CoA, hence Acetyl-CoA is the incorrect answer. The FAD stripping system also produces the FADH2 molecules that enter the electron transport chain and produce ATP. Therefore, if there was no FAD, the production of ATP would also cease. The lack of availability of FAD would have a domino effect on the entire beta-oxidation pathway. The correct answer is A.
